quarterly_data.signal: First quarter ever above $3 billion of revenue: Q2 revenue was $3.3 billion, an increase of $1.1 billion, with 44% same-store revenue growth; electrical segment revenue grew 81% and mechanical segment revenue increased 40%. EPS of $12.53 was up 92% year over year; EBITDA rose 80% to $600 million and operating margin surged to 17.1% from 13.8%.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 revenue $3.3 billion (same-store +44%); electrical +81%, mechanical +40%; EPS $12.53 (+92%); EBITDA $600 million (+80%)

quarterly_data.signal: Technology (data centers, included in industrial) was 58% of revenue, a substantial increase from 40% in the prior year; industrial customers accounted for 75% of total revenue in the first half of 2026 and remain the major drivers of pipeline and backlog. New-building construction was 75% of revenue and modular was 17% of revenue year-to-date.
quarterly_data.figure: technology 58% of revenue (vs 40% prior year); industrial 75%; modular 17% YTD

quarterly_data.signal: Backlog reached a record $14.1 billion, up $5.9 billion or 73% year over year ($5.6 billion same-store) and up $1.6 billion or 13% sequentially; same-store backlog entering Q3 is 69% higher than a year ago. Q2 bookings were especially strong in the technology sector in both construction and modular; modular alone booked $510 million net above what it burned.
quarterly_data.figure: backlog $14.1 billion (+73% YoY, +13% QoQ); same-store backlog +69%; modular net bookings $510 million

quarterly_data.signal: Modular capacity: over 3.5 million sq ft of building capacity is dedicated to modular today, on track for more than 4 million sq ft in production by year-end and approximately 5 million sq ft by late summer 2027. The expansion is overwhelmingly for existing customers and orders - the two hyperscalers Comfort works with continue to provide multi-year volume commitments, which is the condition for adding space; CapEx is about 5% of revenue and a recent building purchase was $100 million.
quarterly_data.figure: modular capacity 3.5 million sq ft now, >4 million sq ft by YE2026, ~5 million sq ft by late summer 2027; CapEx ~5% of revenue

quarterly_data.signal: 2026 same-store revenue growth is expected to finish in the mid- to high-30% range (through six months it has grown 47%), implying second-half growth in the high 20s to low 30s against heavy Q4 comparables; gross profit margins are expected to continue in the strong ranges averaged in recent quarters (Q2 gross margin 25.9% vs 23.5%).
quarterly_data.figure: 2026 same-store growth mid- to high-30%; 1H same-store +47%; Q2 gross margin 25.9%

quarterly_data.signal: Comfort sells directly to the hyperscalers and the most important intermediaries and reports a very deep and calm certainty among them that they will keep building, with no sign of a letdown; it has established itself as a provider to one of the hyperscalers and is running small pilot contracts with frontier labs and co-location providers in modular that could lead to future programs. Customers are inducing other builders because they want more modular product than Comfort will build, not to replace it.

Free cash flow was $999 million in the quarter (about 2.5x earnings), helped by advanced cash from customers locking up Comfort's capacity ahead of when costs are incurred - management calls the advanced cash an indicator of how much counterparties value locking up capacity right now; net cash position is over $1.8 billion. Comfort only takes work it can perform and does detailed labor planning so it does not out-kick its coverage.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 free cash flow $999 million; net cash over $1.8 billion

quarterly_data.signal: Hunt Electric acquisition (Utah electrical contractor) closed May 1st and is expected to contribute about $250 million of annualized revenue, pairing with Comfort's mechanical subsidiaries in that market; on data-center moratoriums (e.g. New York), management says backlog work was already planned and permitted and that these data centers will get built somewhere, subject to getting the power.
